items.summary: Large multimodal models (LMMs) are increasingly deployed as agents that perceive, reason, and act in interactive multi-agent environments. items.summary: As AI agents become increasingly connected through networks and take on tasks that require negotiation and joint decision-making, a systematic approach is needed to assess how their views converge and what information supports their decisions. items.summary: Large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems (MASs) solve complex tasks through interacting agents, yet their reliability is difficult to analyze because failures depend on both individual agents and how information and errors propagate across the system. items.summary: These notes are based on our reading of Michael Nielsen's online book neuralnetworksanddeeplearning.com. items.title: The Wandering Must Continue: Pure Mathematicians as Rangers of the North
items.summary: Pure mathematics is an honest barometer of a civilization's scientific capacity, maintaining an unwritten culture of rigor, intellectual honesty, and precision whose primary service is not merely theorems, but human judgment. In an era of automated theorem generation and formal verification, this essay argues that establishing a result and understanding why it holds remain distinct achievements that require deliberate institutional protection.

items.title: The crisis of AI-generated mathematics
items.summary: In this essay, I present the case for total opposition to the use of artificial intelligence in mathematics. I offer proposals for how individuals, departments, journals, and institutions can act in concert to make sure that mathematics survives the coming crisis.

items.summary: Intelligent agent interactions in real-world web environments are commonly constrained by request budgets, time delays, anti-crawling restrictions, and operational failure risks. items.summary: We introduce a predictive world model for electronic health records (EHR) that represents patient histories as action conditioned latent trajectories. items.summary: Tabular data are prevalent across diverse domains such as healthcare and finance. Zero-shot tabular learning aims to make predictions without labeled data. items.summary: Fake accounts continue to undermine online platforms, yet it remains unclear whether multimodal learning offers meaningful improvements over strong metadata baselines or graph-based approaches. items.summary: Native NVFP4 promises to accelerate reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs), but achieving stable learning across separate training and sampling engines remains challenging. items.title: Beyond Prediction: A Component-Level Study of Concept Recovery in In-Context Learning
items.summary: In-context learning (ICL) enables language models to make accurate predictions from demonstrations, but prediction success alone does not reveal the extent to which the underlying concept has been recovered.
